title: Right, After the Hedge
scene: Wind at dawn on a Kent residential that dead-ends into a T. You need the right. A hedge on the corner eats the sidewalk sightline. Your blinker has been on for a block because Deac's voice in your head still counts cadence. A cyclist you cannot yet see will be on that sidewalk if this is that kind of morning. The DOL wants you past the hedge's blind before you commit the nose. The Menace's plow makes every early turn longer than it looks.
decision: The hedge hides the right sidewalk. When do you start the turn?

options.text: Start the turn at the hedge so you can peek the sidewalk with the plow
options.result: The plow is in the crosswalk before you can see it. Marisol is not here this time. A kid on a scooter is. You freeze with steel in his path. He stops. You have taught the corner that cars occupy the sidewalk to see.

options.text: Cut the corner tight to stay out of whoever is on the far side
options.result: You take the turn in their sidewalk. The knobbies climb the curb. The plow rings off a fire hydrant nobody has painted in a year. Tight was not smaller. Tight was on the wrong side of the geometry.

options.text: Skip the turn and go left around the block where you can see
options.result: You kill a blinker that had been telling the truth and take an unsignaled left at a T. The through car you did not have honks. You make the block. You also skipped the skill the corner was for.

options.text: Stop at the sidewalk line, search around the hedge, then turn into the nearest right lane
options.result: You stop short of the sidewalk. The hedge still hides a slice. You creep until the slice is a view. Empty. You take the nearest right lane, wide enough that the plow does not climb the curb. The blinker dies when the wheel unwinds. Boring. Correct.

debrief: Right turns yield to the sidewalk and crosswalk first. If a hedge eats the sightline, stop and search before the nose occupies it. Finish in the nearest right lane. Cutting the corner puts you on the sidewalk you were trying to protect.

source.psdp_skill: Skill five: driving on a quiet street – part two
source.teaching_target: Before a right turn, search the sidewalk and crosswalk; do not start the turn until the path is visible; recover into the nearest right lane.

image_brief.subject: high overhead of a residential T: the faded matte-pink VW Beetle on the stem, right blinker implied, plow still short of the sidewalk, a tall live hedge eating the right-corner sightline
image_brief.foreground: faded crosswalk paint across the top of the stem; the sidewalk line the plow has not crossed
image_brief.midground: the nearest right-lane recovery path empty and wide enough for the Beetle; hedge leaves moving in the dawn wind
image_brief.background: Kent houses and chain-link, hard dawn overcast, wet pavement, no other moving cars
image_brief.read: right-turn path still short of the sidewalk; the hedge hides the crosswalk — turn geometry before the nose occupies it

geometry.ego_nose_in_frame: the plow blade points toward the top of the frame
